articleTitle: A Masked Autoencoder -Based Approach for Defect Classification in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, automatic defect classification is of paramount importance. Even the slightest defects can compromise chip performance or lead to complete failure, subsequently impacting chip yield rates. Currently, defect classification still heavily relies on manual processes, often leading to a significant number of misclassifications. In this paper, we propose a method based on MAE (Masked Autoencoder) for automatic defect classification in chip manufacturing. The core concept of MAE involves applying a high-proportion random mask to images, creating a challenging image reconstruction task. Using the unmasked image patches, the model predicts the masked patches for self-supervised pretraining. When applied to downstream tasks, this methodology enhances the model's generalization and feature representation capabilities. In a task-agnostic way, we conduct self-supervised pretraining on a large number of SEM (Scanning Electron Microscope) images without the necessity of any labels. In a task-specific way, we fine-tune the network using a limited amount of highly reliable labels. Experimental results suggest that our method is capable of accurately classifying defects with minimal labeled data, greatly reducing labor costs.

articleTitle: Line edge roughness analysis and simulation at advanced litho process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Line edge roughness is the deviation of a feature edge from its ideal shape and is defined as three times the standard deviation. The deviation from the average line width is defined as line width roughness. As feature sizes shrink with Moore's Law, critical dimension variations caused by roughness cannot be ignored. Variations in transistor gate length can result in transistor leakage, and large distributions in transistor gate length can lead to large variations in transistor speed. From a process standpoint, the presence of roughness renders it more challenging to attain precise process control during manufacturing. In the lithography process, LER and LWR depend on several parameters, such as critical dimension, pitch, photoresist and its processing, source mask optimizations, focus, energy, etc. Therefore, an in-depth understanding of the roughness mechanisms is important for improving roughness. This paper has studied the interdependencies through the utilization of simulation techniques, and correlated with the measured roughness, using different critical dimension and pitch patterns. In consequence, a roughness mechanism has been obtained. The simulation can also predict roughness changes at other conditions to improve it.

articleTitle: Photolithography Hotspot Detection Based on Deep Learning LHD Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Raising pattern density on the integrated circuit layout enables reduction of the chip size and cost, while fabrication becomes more difficult. Both number and type of hotspot are increasing during the scaling down. Hotspot detection usually relies on photolithography simulation, that consumes large number of massive computational resource and often takes a long time. To address these limitations, we propose a lightweight hotspot detection model, the Lithography Hotspot Detection (LHD) model, based on deep learning technology. In order to enhance the training of the model, we employed Mentor Calibre's SONR tool to sample the hotspot and non-hotspot graphics and prepare the input dataset. Experimental results show that the hotspot detection accuracy of the LHD model reaches 95.25%, which is 5.07% higher than that of the traditional classification model Convnext.

articleTitle: Fast imaging model of periodic patterns in plasmonic lithography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: As a new and alternative lithography technology, plasmonic lithography can break through the diffraction limit of traditional lithography by exciting the surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) to make the evanescent wave at the mask participate in imaging. The photoresist aerial image distribution of different mask patterns can be calculated by establishing an imaging model, which is the basis for understanding and further optimizing imaging. Based on the idea of machine learning and linear fitting, a fast imaging model for plasmonic lithography is established, including periodic rectangular hole pattern. Compared with the rigorous numerical method, the fast imaging model can greatly improve the calculation speed with high accuracy, which creates conditions for the development of computational lithography technology.

articleTitle: Metrology Challenge for Monitoring Post CMP Pattern Through CD SEM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: With the increase in semiconductor design and process complexity, the need for manufacturing process monitor is increasing. Optical critical dimension (OCD) spectroscopy is widely used in measurement and control of chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process in semiconductor manufacturing because of its nondestructive and high throughput characteristics. However, due to the limitation of the design at test pad and the shortage of evaluating roughness in image, it has encountered some measurement challenges in monitor post-CMP pattern. Therefore, this work overcomes the weakness of conventional electron beam metrology and comprehensively evaluates the feasibility of critical dimension scanning electron microscopy (CDSEM) for post-CMP stage patterns by testing various beam voltage and currents to optimized imaging as well as a special algorithm to optimized the calculation of critical dimensions.

articleTitle: Simulation study on the robustness of polar mark for incident light polarization states
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In order to improve the alignment accuracy of advanced lithography processes, the polar mark was designed to balance the requirement between pitch size device matching and process uniformity. In this paper, the polar mark is studied using the rigorous coupled wave method, as the period is close to the incident wavelength. The robustness of polar mark for incident light polarization states is investigated. Comparing with segmented alignment mark, the polar mark showed better robustness. And polar mark exhibits high process adaptability. The determination of the polar mark pattern density must be in combination with the process. The wet recess process changes the wafer quality (WQ) of the polar mark. The polar mark with this process still has good polarization robustness. The research content of this paper shows significance in enhancing the alignment performance of lithography.

articleTitle: Test Pattern Sampling Methodology for Model Tuning Efficiency and Robustness Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Optical proximity effect correction (OPC) is an important part of the integrated circuit fabrication process to prevent the device electrical properties from being affected by pattern distortion caused by optical proximity effect. Accurate correction requires high simulation accuracy and robustness of the OPC model, which needs high coverage of the test patterns over the actual layout. However, in the industry, the test patterns are selected based on experience of engineers, which has the problem of a large number of similar patterns and insufficient coverage over the actual layout. Therefore, in this paper, a sampling method is proposed, which uses clustering algorithms to classify the geometric and optical features of the test patterns. According to the classification results, redundant patterns are removed and the coverage of the test patterns is increased, which will shorten the modeling period and improve the model robustness.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transformer-Based Approach for DUV Lithography SEM Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Traditional Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) image noise reduction techniques, such as frame averaging or utilizing higher resolution SEM images, may result in potential electron beam damage and could also limit the speed of screening. In this paper, we propose a deep-learning-based denoising method using a Transformer-based architecture that addresses these challenges. This method effectively reduces noise while preserving image details, providing comparable measurements such as line width roughness that are only attainable with higher signal-to-noise ratio SEM images.

articleTitle: A Rigorous-Simulation-Driven OPC Solution Was Built Before Obtaining Real Wafer Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In the development of advanced semiconductor processes, photolithography is an extremely crucial step. On one hand, the design layout needs to be transferred to the silicon wafer with an accurate computational lithography solution, requiring a long development cycle. On the other hand, a structure wafer needs to be generated as early as possible for optimal tuning by other process modules. However, due to natural process sequences, these two aspects usually cannot be synchronized. Therefore, how to synchronize these two aspects to shorten the process cycle is a research hotspot for researchers. This article proposes a method based on S-Litho rigorous simulation in the absence of real wafer measurement results. By generating mask structures that are close to actual production situations in the early stages of process development, OPC solutions can be established in advance to accelerate process development and optimization work. In addition, when the process is still uncertain, rigorous simulation can assist in optimizing relevant parameters. Establishing an OPC solution using simulation data provided by S-Litho can accelerate process development. Meanwhile, after obtaining real wafer measurement data in the future, the differences between simulation data and wafer data can be evaluated to determine whether the model needs to be re-adjusted or processed by using biasing methods. In short, establishing an OPC solution through rigorous simulation is the most practical solution to the actual process before real data is available. While providing optimal tuning for other process modules, it can also accelerate the establishment of formal computational lithography solutions.

articleTitle: The Ultimate Step to Predict Yield Impact from Mask by Litho Printability Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Comprehensive mask inspection is a common but critical method for wafer fab process control and yield management. With full adoption of Resolution Enhancement Technology (RET) and Source Mask Optimization (SMO) techniques, post-inspection defect review and dispositioning has become much more challenging than before. It is very time consuming and difficult to consistently pick out all wafer-printable defects on mask by manual operation. Our previous work introduced a systematic solution to handle this situation. In this paper, we focus on the ultimate step to predict critical dimension (CD) impact by utilizing a technology called lithography printable review (LPR). We will not only explain the idea of LPR workflow, but also discuss the three key challenges to apply LPR and how to address them. With more than two years verification, LPR is adopted as a trustable solution to secure zero yield impact from mask.

articleTitle: The Rational Photomask Layout Design of Vias for Application in Double Patterning UV Photolithography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Due to the optical diffraction limit, the resolution of conventional UV photolithography is around ~1 micron, which hinders its potential in sub-micron patterning for broader applications. Efforts have been made to overcome the diffraction limit, such as double/multiple patterning photolithography. Recently, a derivative of UV photolithography called dual-layer photolithography was reported can generate sub-micron linear patterns. In addition to linear patterns, here, we report a double patterning method to get via patterns using dual-layer photolithography. The photomask design rule for double patterning dual-layer photolithography is studied and presented in this work. For demonstration purpose, an example GDSII via file from practical application contains> 10,000 vias was used. The vias with original size of 4 μm would be reduced to 300 nm after the double patterning process.

articleTitle: Design of A Large Field of View High Numerical Aperture Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Illumination System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: The illumination system of extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) is the core of extreme ultraviolet lithography. The illumination system is responsible for providing a variety of complex off-axis illumination modes, and illuminating the mask with high uniformity. In this paper, a design of high numerical aperture (NA) anamorphic EUV illumination system with large field of view is completed. Simulation results show that the system can satisfied the requirements of high uniformity on the mask under different illumination modes.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 420GHz highly scaled InAlN/GaN HEMTs by Electron Beam Lithography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: GaN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) are promising candidates for millimeter wave amplifiers above 100 GHz for 6G communications. To satisfy those requirements, a maximum oscillation frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{f}_{\max})$</tex> surpassing 400 GHz is essential, necessitating the deployment of advanced down-scaling and patterning technologies. Through the utilization of electron beam lithography, ultra-scaled InAlN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire with T-gates with gate length of~60 nm and source-drain distance of~300 nm were fabricated, reaching <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\max}$</tex> over 420 GHz with a corresponding f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>exceeding 150 GHz. To the best of the author's knowledge, these scaled HEMTs exhibit the highest fmax among reported HEMTs on sapphire.

articleTitle: Pix2PixHD-Based Generation of SEM Image in the ETCH Domain by SEM Image of LITHO Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, a forward etching process model that can accurately predict the pattern transformation from post-lithography (ADI) to post-etch (AEI) is greatly desired. However, current etching model is etch bias based, it is unable to offer rich information as the SEM image does for engineers to do wafer disposition. We propose an AEI image generation model using the Pix2PixHD. It can generate AEI images corresponding to ADI images. Experimental results demonstrate that our generated images achieve a SSIM of 96.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and a MSSIM of 94.2% when compared to AEI images. Therefore, Our method can generate AEI images with a high resolution of (1024, 1024) and meet the requirements of applications.

articleTitle: Feature Point-Based Proximity Effect Correction of Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: The proximity effect correction (PEC) of patterns has significant applications in electron beam lithography (EBL) systems that cannot adjust dosage arbitrarily. This paper proposes a PEC method that discretizes the pattern into feature points and compensates for the proximity effect by changing the shape of the design through the movement of these feature points. This method enables PEC for arbitrary patterns, and the precision of the PEC can be tuned by adjusting parameters such as the density of the feature points. Experimental verification of this method was conducted, and the results were consistent with expectations.

articleTitle: Exploration charge effect and wafer backside materials correlation to Diamond-Like Carbon wafer table degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In DRAM process development history, Wafer table (WT) corrosion is an inevitable problem which mainly affects exposed wafer focus and overlay in exposure machines. In this study, Diamond-Like Carbon (DLC) WT experience of the Vendor Charge Measurements (VCM) and Wafer Load Grid (WLG) characterization elaborated correlation among WT corrosion, charge effect and wafer backside materials, contributing to extend WT lifetime and improve high-volume manufacturing (HVM) stability. Research results indicated CXMT product clustered charge main from pre-lithography process and Lithography back side treatment (BST) process. The difference of wafer backside materials bring friction in varying degrees between wafer and WT. The wafer backside materials with hardness and smooth property induced WT rapid degradation.

articleTitle: A Curvilinear OPC Workflow for Highly Repetitive Structures and High Aspect Ratio Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In this study, a workflow based on curvilinear OPC (CLOPC) & memory OPC (MEMOPC) is introduced. In the workflow, the curvilinear-based method is applied on highly repetitive structures and high aspect ratio patterns. Three CLOPC solutions and two RLOPC solutions for an iso dot are studied. The results show that curvilinear masks give more flexible correction control than RLOPC and ILT. Mask shapes can be controlled from regular ones to aggressive ones, using Calibre nmCLOPC. The most aggressive mask improves corner rounding but leads to lower lithographic performance. A test case with highly repetitive structures and limited design rule is studied. Three solutions to the test case are generated, which are called as regular CLOPC, aggressive CLOPC and RLOPC. The properties of simulated resists, which include ILS/NILS/MEEF/PVBand/DOF, are compared respectively. When using a regular CLOPC solution, the lithographic performance is better than aggressive CLOPC and RLOPC. The total runtime of combined workflow reduces 38.6%, compared with isolated CLOPC flow. It could be an effective approach to enhance the key layer's process window.

articleTitle: Application of Genetic Algorithm to Solving Better SRAF Rules
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Sub-resolution assist feature (SRAF) is critical to the process window for lithography in advanced integrated circuit manufacturing. SRAF provides a large enhancement to the process window (PW) of isolated (ISO) pattern. Currently, the SRAF rule is determined through the design of experiments (DOE) method in the industry. This method can only optimize one or two parameters at a time, but the SRAF problem needs to solve at least three parameters. In this paper, the genetic algorithm (GA) with improved selection method, which is highly efficient in multi-parameter optimization, is combined with lithography model and Calibre OPCVerify tool to determine the SRAF rule. A much shorter rule setup cycle is achieved by using GA, with a better performance in process window enhancement.

articleTitle: A transmissive spectral purity filter for suppressing infrared radiation in extreme ultraviolet lithography source
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: We propose a transmissive spectral purity filter (SPF) with rectangular fishnet structures for laser-produced plasma extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography source. Such a transmissive SPF consists of a graphene-based thin membrane carrying a Molybdenum absorber pattern for the infrared (IR) radiation suppression. By using using the rigorous coupled wave analysis method, we investigate the optical properties of the transmissive SPF and optimize the structure parameters to suppress the out-of-band IR radiation. We analyze the dependence of the transparency at wavelength of 13.5 nm and infrared radiation suppression on the structure parameters. Theoretical analysis reveals that the transmittance at undesirable wavelength of 10.6μm is as low as 0.11%, while maintaining the in-band EUV transmittance as 75.92%, thereby enabling full separation of EUV and IR radiation from the EUV light source for high volume manufacturing lithography. Especially, the light incident angle on SPF has very little influence on both EUV and IR transmittances, thereby relaxing placement requirements significantly.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of spot sizes on Optical critical dimension measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: With the rapid reduction of the dimensions of nanostructure, optical critical dimension(OCD) measurement has been paid more and more attention. In this paper, the effect of measuring spot size using OCD on nanostructure measurements was investigated. The relationship between different spot sizes in PAD and the MSE of the simulated spectrum and experimental spectrum is verified by experiments. These results provide empirical support for the subsequent design of OCD tools with high productivity and application value.

articleTitle: Contact Hole Multiplication by Directed Self-Assembly of Block Copolymer with Homopolymer-Blending
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Directed self-assembly (DSA) of cylindrical block copolymers (BCPs) with graphoepitaxy demonstrates great promise in contact hole multiplication at sub-7 nm technology nodes. However, achieving defect-free device patterns with conventional lithography remains a significant challenge. This study aims to investigate the impact of blending homopolymer polystyrene (PS) with BCP on the self-assembly behavior within confined elliptical spaces. Comprehensive experimental and simulation studies were conducted to examine different BCP blending systems. The results demonstrate that introducing homopolymer PS enables the formation of defect-free bi-pore structures in elongated elliptical template holes. Therefore, blending a homopolymer PS with BCP provides valuable insights for advanced lithography techniques, facilitating the fabrication of high-quality patterns at sub-7 nm technology nodes.

articleTitle: Selecting test patterns with the pool-based sampling method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: A precisely calibrated process model is required for the optical proximity correction purpose. To fit the model, a test pattern mask needs to be prepared and the lithographic experiment should be done. It is beneficial to select fewer test patterns without compromising the accuracy of the lithographic model fit with them. We apply the autoencoder and core set method to select parts of gauges out from the existing test patterns set. The models obtained with the selected data achieve nearly the same precision on the original set of test patterns compared with the model fit by the whole set data.

articleTitle: A Novel Feedforward and Feedback Method for Overlay Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Overlay (OVL) is one of the most critical process control parameters required to enable successful semiconductor manufacturing and the specifications for on-product overlay (OPO) have become much tighter in today's advanced technology nodes. To ensure overlay performance meets the required product specifications, a combination of feedforward and feedback run-to-run approaches have been adopted to minimize Iot-to-Iot variations to better control OPO. In this work, we utilize traditional feedforward correction techniques used to compensate for non-alignment overlay, but also incorporate and leverage other fingerprints which can also impact overlay. Our new method selects the feedforward layer based on multiple metrology and process indicators and demonstrates significant improvement compared to the current solution.

articleTitle: BOE-ziSIM: A Design-Technology-Manufacturing Co-optimization Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Thin-film transistors (TFT) and organic light-emitting diodes (OLED) for display applications involve new materials, structures and processes in the design and development phase, and these elements can have a significant impact on the performance of the TFT devices. The increasing need for personalized and diversified display productions brings two problems: 1. To achieve the desired performance indicators in fabrication processes, a large number of experiments are required to continuously optimize the process parameters, which not only increases economic and time costs but also limits the development speed of new productions. 2. The display production iterations are getting faster to meet the market requirement, in other words, the time left for yield improvement becomes shorter. A Design-Technology-Manufacturing Co-optimization platform called BOE-ziSIM is introduced in this paper, it was developed to solve the above mentioned problems, the experiment results show that the defects analysis time is reduced from hours to minutes, and the equipment adjustment time is reduced from days to minutes.

articleTitle: An Approach to Extracting SRAF Rules from Inverse Lithography Technology Results
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Inserting sub-resolution assist feature (SRAF) has great effect on improving the process window. Rule-based SRAF (RBSRAF) provides full chip application but its performance and development time mainly depends on experience. Inverse lithography technology (ILT) provides SRAF that significantly enhance the process window, but it takes too long for full chip application. In order to achieve SRAF performance close to ILT process, meanwhile keep the high processing speed of RBSRAF, we propose an approach to extract SRAF rules from ILT results, trying to insert ILT-like RBSRAF. The type of geometry parameters extracted from the ILT results refer to the variability of SRAF rules, namely the editable configurations in Calibre nmSRAF tool. The extracted rule has achieved significant process window enhancement in 55nm contact layer in a much shorter processing time, as compared to that of experience-based RBSRAF.

articleTitle: Implementing an OPC-based Analysis Method for Evaluating the Capabilities of Photoresist and Identifying Hot Spots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Photoresist is an essential material in integrated circuit technology, playing a pivotal role in determining the quality and defects of the lithography process. Traditional assessment methods, which involve subjective analysis of the exposure focus-energy matrix, only provide limited data and one-dimensional graphics, hindering the ability to predict hot spots in actual production layouts. This paper introduces a novel photoresist evaluation technique called Optical-Resist Delta (ORD). By utilizing the OPC method to calculate the difference in evaluation indicators for various structures under optical and resist models, ORD enables a more accurate and qualitative determination of photoresist applicability. Moreover, it predicts hot spots in real layouts and simplifies the photoresist selection process for fab, making it effortless as choosing products. This method incorporates a wide range of photoresist types, diverse structural graphics, and real fab wafer data, offering a straightforward and high-precision solution.

articleTitle: Extending DRSEM Inspection Capacities and Applications with the Introduction of D2DB Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: The rapid evolution of semiconductor process technologies has made defect detection using Defect Review Scanning Electron Microscopy (DRSEM) increasingly challenging, especially for defects in complex patterned regions. By integrating design layout data into the detection process, we have enhanced DRSEM's defect detectability and expanded its applications. The D2DB technology allows for accurate detection of systematic defects within patterned areas. In addition, it aids in identifying various soft defects and those arising from pattern drift. The technique's target recognition capability also facilitates direct monitoring of CD variations and hotspot verification by combining SEM review results with design layout checks.

articleTitle: Theoretical Review of a new approach of Lithography at nm Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: This article theoretically reviews the new potential offered for photolithography by the combination of 2 elements: EIT (Electromagnetically Induced Transparency) and SMLM (Single Molecule Localization Microscopy), lithography with nm resolution is expected, with outstanding advantage. Light resonant with atomic transition frequency, when pass through with assistance of couple light, quantum coherent interference will cause previously opaque medium to induce sharp transparent windows in the frequency absorption region, while exhibiting slow light effects. Microscopy is lens system like photolithography, its limit is dictated by Airy disk, with value of 200nm, SMLM has brought inspiration, it breaks through limit and achieve nm resolution.

articleTitle: Metrology Evaluation Indicators of Gate Line End Patterning of SRAM by Using SEM Contour Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Critical dimension scanning electron microscope (CDSEM) is a crucial tool for measuring the dimensions of patterns, enabling sub-nanometer precision measurements after lithography and etching processes on wafers. However, the measurements performed by CDSEM are focused on a single process layer, and the measurement types are limited. Which makes it difficult to comprehensively evaluate the overall pattern process by considering adjacent layers. In this study, several evaluation indicators are proposed for the gate and active area (AA) stack layer structure of static random-access memory (SRAM) by using CDSEM contour extraction and graphical calculations. This research realizes more sensitive evaluation standards, which can be utilized in the Statistical Process Control system (SPC) of semiconductor fabrication to enhance pattern process control.

articleTitle: Solutions to Calibration Errors of OPC Models for Special Pattern Below 40 NM Nodes*
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: The accuracy of OPC (Optical Proximity effect Correction, OPC) model is closely related to product yield. An accurate OPC model is the guarantee of successful development and mass production yield. However, for some special pattern, the fitting results cannot be changed even if their weight is increased. This paper is investigated the special pattern fitting error and we find out the reasons for this behavior of OPC model and give solutions. The OPC model is resist model of synopsys, and use progen as model building tool.

articleTitle: Investigation of Multiple Feedforward Modes for On Product Overlay Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing process, large lot to lot (L2L) variation induced by multiple process steps is a big challenge for On-Product Overlay (OPO) control. Feedforward control has been proven to be an effective method to handle such a variation. However, different feedforward modes are needed depending on alignment and overlay schemes of the layers. In this paper, we report an investigation of using suitable feedforward modes for OPO control of a number of critical layers from a logic node. Different feedforward modes are defined according to differences in alignment and overlay tree to ensure the best results. Besides commonly used correction feedforward in semiconductor industry, we implement also de-correction fingerprint feedforward to some layers. We identify also that for some layers using partial feedforward is better than feedforwarding the whole correction or de-correction fingerprints. Our results show that combination of feedforward and feedback control is able to improve OPO by 40%~70% comparing to feedback-only one. With such a large improvement, the fab can reduce the number of pilot-run layers by 84%. This saves cost significantly. Integrating the aforementioned multiple feedforward control modes into the fab automation system has also been realized.

articleTitle: Nanosheet Count Optimization Strategy of Complementary FET (CFET) Scaling Beyond 2 nm From Device to Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Complementary Field-Effect Transistors is one of the most promising structures for replacing GAA (Gate-All-Around) field-effect transistors while continuing the advancement of Moore's Law. Thus, optimizing its structure is a crucial research direction. This study proposes a nano-sheet count design strategy to address the issue of mismatched electron and hole mobilities in standard CFET cell and a nine-stage ring oscillator (RO). The simulation results demonstrate the effective matching of electron and hole mobilities by adjusting the ratio of NMOS (n-type) and PMOS (p-type) nano-sheet counts, thus enabling the optimization of circuit performance and power consumption for specific applications. In the CFET of the RO unit, a frequency increase of 10% and a capacitance reduction of 6% are achieved with only a 3% increase in power consumption, comparing a CFET with four P-doped nano-sheet channels and two N -doped nano-sheet channels to one with three P-doped nano-sheet channels and three N-doped nano-sheet channels.

articleTitle: An Optical Critical Dimension (OCD) Study with Standard Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Optical Critical Dimension (OCD) technique, also known as optical scatterometry, is designed to obtain three-dimensional periodic optical information from device architectures and has achieved great success in IC industry over the past decades. Because it is not image based, OCD technique is not constrained by the diffraction effects that limit image resolution. The major benefit of optical scatterometry is that it can provide rich geometrical information, i.e., CD, SWA, trench depth, film thickness, in one quick single measurement. Furthermore, it provides measurement data with the benefit of none-destruction and high throughput, and thus can be used to acquire in-line measurement data with high-sampling. In our previous work, we have reported OCD model building method and model verification procedures. Then, what is the limit of this metrology method? In this paper, we will study the response of OCD model to a few standard structures in order to understand the mechanism of OCD signal response within the theoretical framework of optical ellipsometry, which can be used as a basis for the understanding of its extendability to the detection of smaller, thinner, more refractive structures in future technology nodes.

articleTitle: An Innovative Lithography Process Window Decision Based On Aggregation of Multi Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Automated image analysis and image classification system that based on machine learning have been developed and applied to the PWQ/FEM flow to enhance process stability and accuracy. Moving these task from artificial to automation has the added benefit of avoiding person-to-person inconsistencies in classification. In this paper, we approach a data flow consists of an automated machine learning-enabled process window analysis system that relies on CDSEM images taken on a Focus/Exposure Matrix wafer. Combined systematic data preprocessing and aggregation of multi machine learning approaches, we improved the accuracy of the process window analysis over 94%.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Scale Feature Learning-Based Residual Network Improves Semiconductor Wafer Defect Classification Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Wafer inspection is a crucial step in the semiconductor manufacturing process. Accurate inspection of wafer defects is of great significance in ensuring chip quality, improving production efficiency, and reducing cost losses. However, most wafer defects are irregular and tiny which brings great challenges to defect inspection. At present, most wafer defect inspection is also inefficient and has low accuracy. Addressing this, a novel wafer defect classification algorithm based on the residual network was proposed in this study. The algorithm proposes a multi-scale feature learning block that can obtain finer-grained features and distinguish different types of defects as the network depth increases. The performance of this algorithm was evaluated using the MixedWM38 dataset of semiconductor wafers and a classification accuracy of 99.13% was achieved, demonstrating competitive results when compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Improve photomask writing error using Registration Correction (RegC) technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Photomask writing error (aka Registration) is a key quality index in mask manufacture process, representing the position placement errors between the actual pattern and design pattern. A small part of writing error can be corrected by scanner iHOPC (intra-field High Order Process Correction), and the uncorrected part is the residual. Obviously, the residual will contribute to wafer overlay directly. To resolve the challenging topic, a novel photomask writing error correction technology named Carl Zeiss For Tune Registration Correction (RegC), which innovatively develops mask expansion tuning process, is given great expectations. In this work, we demonstrate an optimized operation mode and sampling scheme to improve writing error effectively using RegC technology. First of all, benefiting from the optimization by all kinds of operation mode comprehensively, the best registration correction results can be achieved. More importantly, we report an innovative approach towards the sampling scheme for RegC. We figure out that the best sampling scheme is the combination of the frame registration mark and In Die main design pattern. Owing to the above work, the registration residual can be improved remarkably. This work brings fresh insights into the efficient solution for mask writing error improvement by RegC.

articleTitle: An Algorithm to Reduce Coloring Conflicts for Triple Patterning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Due to the resolution limitations of 193nm DUV lithography, design layers with minimum pitch below 78nm can no longer be patterned with a single mask. As technology nodes continue to advance, starting from 16nm nodes some design layers would need to be decomposed into multiple masks so that the smallest dimension from each mask can be large enough for single-mask patterning. Triple Patterning, using three masks, has then been considered a viable option. However, decomposing a mask into three turns into a graph-coloring problem which is NP complete. This paper describes a coloring approach by which the mask is first colored using a greedy coloring algorithm such as Welsh-Powell (WP), and since it does not (and no algorithm does) guarantee chromatic coloring, an algorithm is proposed to resolve its coloring conflicts if found.

articleTitle: New Strategy to Improve the Measurement Accuracy of Asymmetrical Mark Caused by Process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: As the process development is getting tighten, the requirement of process to alignment and overlay Mark gets more and more strict. The accuracy of a Mark measurement plays an important role in semiconductor manufacturing. However, process step in CMP (Chemical Mechanical Planarization), etch and deposition all can contribute to disadvantage impacts and then influence alignment and overlay mark performance. So, how can we determine the accuracy of our measurements? In this study, we focus on different CMP behavior showing a clear expansion map for alignment and overlay mark. By applying default mark under given segment condition, the dishing effect caused by CMP can be significantly improved. At the same time, Mark asymmetry caused by CMP can be significantly reduced by various optimal color weight (OCW) measurements. These behaviors greatly improve the stability of On-Product overlay(OPO), and the rework rate is reduced by 30% on product wafers.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin Film Metrology Technique: Grazing Incident X-Ray Fluorescence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Thickness measurements for a couple of atomic layer ultra-thin nitride and high-K dielectric materials (TaN, TiN, HfOx) were performed using our self-developed instrument, the ÅX- T100,via grazing incident x-ray fluorescence (GIXRF). Single-site repeatability results demonstrate that our instrument exhibits excellent precision with CV%=0.09%. An analysis of the wafer mapping results including 49 data points indicates a wafer thickness uniformity (uniformity %) of less than 3%. Considering the features of the x-ray fluorescence technique, which include non-invasiveness, immunity to surface oxidation, applicability to both metals and dielectrics, and suitability for transparent and opaque materials, GIXRF stands out as a perfect non-invasive metrology tool for measuring ultra-thin film thickness and composition at the angstrom level.

articleTitle: Rigorous Simulation for Impact of Self-Aligned Multiple Patterning on Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: As integrated circuit evolve to lower technology node, alignment accuracy of mask to wafer is required to reach sub-nanometer scales to meet production overlay requirements. While, to accommodate shrinking technology node, processes such as self-aligned multiple patterning (SAMP) are developed, which have negative effect on alignment signal strength and generate alignment accuracy errors. In order to avoid possible alignment failures in advance, in this study, based on the self-reference interference alignment system, we methodically discuss the influence of different factors on alignment quality for a SAMP process from the perspective of simulation.

articleTitle: Application in lithography inspection of phase basic image registration algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: The etch bias indicating the differences of the pattern critical dimensions (CD) after developing inspection (ADI) and after etching inspection (AEI) are always measured and compensated to improve the patterning process accuracy. An advanced approach with the high efficiency is to subtract the AEI contour polygons from the ADI contour polygons, however, its precondition is to align well the ADI &AEI contours. Considering the shapes of the ADI&AEI contours are almost same except the position shift, the phase basic image registration algorithm can be used to extract the optimal position shift along the x and y directions, then the contours can be aligned easily by the position translation calibration. The proposed method is verified by the inline images measured by the Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). This approach has a wide range application which need the contour or image comparison such as the photo resister qualification, Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) model verify and mask qualification etc.

articleTitle: Lithographic Stepping Trajectory Planning for Residual Vibration Suppression: An Asymmetric S-Curve Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: During the lithographic process, stepping motion enables a rapid switch from one die to another. To meet the throughput requirement of nowadays high-end lithography equipment, the settling time is limited to only several milliseconds, which requires extremely little residual vibration. The design of the traditional symmetric S-curve through the pole-zero placement theory has the ability to eliminate the residual vibration caused by the zero-damping flexible mode. However, the nonzero damping ratio and the imprecisely known resonant frequency will lead to performance degradation. To tackle this issue, this paper further proposes an asymmetric S-curve planning method, which enhances the robustness. This is accomplished by introducing an additional design parameter at the deceleration phase, which adds one more zero to compensate for the pole of the flexible mode. The proposed method has one preferable feature compared to the existing asymmetric S-curve planning method: the method can be utilized to design not only the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order S-curve but also higher order S-curves. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method To Improve Accuracy of the Wavefront Aberration Measurement Technique Based on Principal Component Analysis of Aerial Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Advanced Patterning Solutions (IWAPS)
abstract: Wavefront aberration of projection lens will deteriorate the lithographic imaging performance, shrink the process window, and depress the yield of chips. The wavefront aberration measurement based on principal component analysis of aerial images (AMAI-PCA) is an efficient technique to solve this problem with the advantages of low cost, high speed and reliable accuracy. To apply this technique to advanced process nodes, this paper proposes an optimization method to improve the accuracy of AMAI-PCA. After obtaining the aberration solution by AMAI-PCA, the BFGS quasi-Newton algorithm is used to further optimize the result. The simulation results show a significant improvement in measurement accuracy.
